pairs.difference: B matches the real sunscreen card in the anchor. pairs.difference: A is a bird feeder hung from a tree. The trunk runs through the full card height (box_height 1.0, margin 0, which is within the real range), and the feeder is centered with a park background. B is a teal pot centered on a gas stove, cropped at the bottom by the stovetop, with steam rising toward the top against a yellow tile wall. Both are frontal, centered and cropped by an edge, and both fill a similar share of the card. Framing gives no reason to choose.

pattern: In the lessons, generated cards show the whole object, centered and frontal, with even padding on all sides, and often with extra scenery added around it (rocks around the lighthouse, a full computer setup). Real cards use a tilted three-quarter view, place the hero off-center, and let the card edge crop it, as with the lighthouse base and the desk. On the test pairs, what still gives generated cards away is a hero floating in the dead center of a flat backdrop or concentric rings with uniform margins, and a hero shrunk inside a busy background (p03 board) so the backdrop wins the first read.
